Asset: WELL-0196 (NE-08 Well 196, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 08 Jan 2023 08:00 · Finished: 18 Jan 2023 13:00 · Well stopped for this job: 245 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0196-0012 on 2023-01-05 Report written: 19 Jan 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0196-0012 showed the wellhead at 9.1 °C with the air at 5.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 236 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 189 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0196-002 (WS-06).

  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0196-009

Asset: WELL-0196 (NE-08 Well 196, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 12 Nov 2023 08:00 · Finished: 06 Dec 2023 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 576 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0196-0056 on 2023-11-09 Report written: 06 Dec 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0196-0056 showed the wellhead at 24.6 °C with the air at 18.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 22 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 8 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0196-029

Asset: WELL-0196 (NE-08 Well 196, T200, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 10 May 2026 08:00 · Finished: 20 May 2026 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 250 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0196-0182 on 2026-05-07 Report written: 20 May 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator found an oil puddle under the gearbox. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0196-0182 showed the wellhead at 33.0 °C with the air at 30.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0196-029 (WS-06).
